note: Track pentatonic-positions (guitar-scales), step 7: a run through three positions of the minor pentatonic scale with two slides, each crossing on its own first with its slide notes ringed, then the run to the metronome and in a solo over the 1st and 4th chords. The old tempo stages and the second key are now moves (any key, 60 to 92 bpm), named only as {{=key}} and {{=bpm}}; the chords are tokens counted the long way once, and the {{?key}} line says what stays the same. missing: position-neck's cross shows one crossing between two positions, so the three-position run is told in the text over a plain three-position neck.

exercise.title: A run across three positions
exercise.why: Each position starts on the notes where the one below it ends, so two slides, each along one string, carry a run through three positions without a break.

cells.text:
The neck below shows only the crossing from position 1 to position 2 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale: position 1 on the low strings, position 2 on the high strings. Start on {{1}} on the low E string and climb position 1. On the G string, slide from the ringed {{4}} up to the ringed {{5}} and finish the climb in position 2.
Come back down the same way, sliding from {{5}} down to {{4}}.

The neck below shows the crossing from position 2 to position 3. Climb position 2, slide from the ringed {{5}} up to the ringed {{b7}} on the G string, and finish the climb in position 3.
This slide is one fret longer than the first, so listen for {{b7}} and stop the slide there.

Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Under it are positions 1, 2 and 3 together. Climb position 1 from the low {{1}}, slide from {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string, then from {{1}} to {{b3}} on the B string, and finish at the top of position 3. Come back down the same way, one note per beat.
Practice until the run is in your muscle memory: both slides land on the click without you looking.

The backing track switches between two chords. {{chord:i7}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:iv7}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track. Improvise in {{=key}} minor pentatonic, and take the run across all three positions in the middle of a phrase.
{{?key}}In another key the frets are new, but the slides are still {{4}} to {{5}} and {{1}} to {{b3}}.

chords.approach: land on its root on beat 1
